props.title: Sweet Smell of Success
props.initialSlug: Scandal at the top of the heap.

sections.content: Sweet Smell of Success (1957) revolutionized film noir with its caustic portrayal of media manipulation and moral corruption. Tony Curtis shattered his pretty-boy image as desperate press agent Sidney Falco, while Burt Lancaster's J.J. Hunsecker towers as one of cinema's most chilling power brokers. The film's razor-sharp dialogue from Ernest Lehman and Clifford Odets ("I'd hate to take a bite outta you. You're a cookie full of arsenic") set a new standard for Hollywood verbal warfare. Director Alexander Mackendrick and cinematographer James Wong Howe transformed Manhattan into a neon-lit nightmare where ethics go to die. The Big Combo|1955|A police lieutenant battles a crime boss in this noir featuring similarly stark black-and-white cinematography|Prime Ace in the Hole|1951|Kirk Douglas stars as an unscrupulous journalist exploiting a cave-in tragedy|Criterion Network|1976|TV news satire about media manipulation and rating chasing|HBO Max

The film's influence on media-focused noir extends through decades of Hollywood storytelling. All the President's Men (1976) borrowed its paranoid atmosphere for journalism drama, while L.A. Confidential (1997) directly referenced Hunsecker's gossip column power in its Sid Hudgens character. The toxic mentor-protégé dynamic between Hunsecker and Falco influenced The Devil Wears Prada (2006) and Whiplash (2014), showing how power corrupts across genres and eras.

Mackendrick's direction broke noir conventions by shooting much of the film in actual New York locations, creating a documentary-like authenticity that influenced the coming New Hollywood movement. This techniques shows up in later New York films like Midnight Cowboy (1969) and Taxi Driver (1976). The film's unflinching look at publicity and power dynamics laid groundwork for media critiques like Quiz Show (1994) and Nightcrawler (2014). The Bad and the Beautiful|1952|Hollywood noir about a ruthless producer's rise and fall|TCM Nightcrawler|2014|Modern noir following an amoral freelance crime photographer|Netflix Gone Girl|2014|Dark meditation on media manipulation and public image|Hulu SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Media Critique

Contemporary filmmakers continue drawing from Sweet Smell's playbook. Gone Girl (2014) echoes its themes of media manipulation, while Succession (2018-2023) directly channels Hunsecker's power-broker dynamics into modern media empire storytelling. The film's cynical view of publicity and journalism feels increasingly relevant in our social media age, with films like The Social Network (2010) and Promising Young Woman (2020) carrying its torch of moral ambiguity in pursuit of influence.
